Congratulations on the home purchase, when it all finally goes through. I used to do maintenance for an apartment complex. Foreclosures take a really long time. It sometimes is an unnecessarily long process, not very uncommon for them to take a year or longer. First thing you will want to do is wash all the surfaces. Paint the walls. Get rid of all the carpet. You would be surprised how much stuff is in carpets even if the property was well maintained. If there is going to be work that will generate a lot of dust, make sure to do it before ripping out the carpet. Make sure to get tests done for Lead and Asbestos prior to any work being done on any surface. Asbestos was commonly in walls, ceilings, siding, roofing, and flooring. To even dispose of some waste, you will very likely need a test performed for asbestos at minimum, Lead might be required as well. If going with a company to do those things, make sure to check up on what the test will cost and find an average on how much disposal will cost. Since it seems you will be doing remodeling, you should check on permits. Make sure the house already has permits filed for any remodeling that was already done, make sure the taxes were paid for what your buying. If you do a remodel and it's found they didn't tax you for that bedroom, you may need to pay the back taxes for having that bedroom at minimum, might have to get rid of it at worse.

As for actual ideas, what one person likes might not be that great to everyone else. I personally like the look of wood. I've always been a fan of Ceder but I'm more than fine with any wood grain surfaces. As for counter tops, it's really up to personal tastes. Avoid marble in the kitchen. It looks nice but it's prone to scorch marks. If you want granite, go for granite tile if you don't have the budget for a slab. My father in-law has granite tile for his kitchen counter tops and they look good. Another possibility is crushed quartz. The advantage with crushed quartz is you will have the option for color to fit your personal tastes. It's not cheap by any means, it's cheaper than slab granite.
